newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares close higher in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares close higher in active trading.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher in active trading on Thursday led by a rise in small- and medium-capitalisation stocks, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.61 percent, or 1.47 points, to 242.34 on high all-share turnover of 165 million shekels against 107 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.32 percent higher at 250.22.

"The trading day opened with a lot of activity by options speculators. Total volume in the Meretz (the preliminary computerised trading session in which the index for the January Maof contract was fixed) was a very high 57 million shekels," said Doron Tsur, head of research at Sahar Securities.

"After the expiry of the Maof options the market relaxed and most of the activity was concentrated in small- and medium- capitalisation stocks," Tsur added. "One of positive factors is that foreign investors were very active today buying shares."
"The session opened with mixed trading because of high activity of Maof players. During the day investors gained confidence and the market closed higher," said a trader at Bank Leumi.
"The market has completely recovered from early-week losses. It now seems that the positive momentum will continue for the near future," he said.

Israel Chemicals, the most active share, fell 3.75 percent to 343 agorot on volume of 13.9 million shekels after its subsidiary Perio Products said it had suspended a U.S. share offering slated for next week. A spokesman for the company said officials believed Perio would go public at a higher valuation after the FDA approved the Perio chip, a product designed to fight gum disease.
"It's a very, very strange announcement. They knew a long time ago that if they got FDA approval the price would be higher," Tsur said.

Other active shares included Koor Industries, which closed unchanged at 32,019 agorot on turnover of 7.8 million shekels, and Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which gained 0.25 percent to 1,824 agorot on volume of 7.5 million shekels.
